questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does this isosceles triangle have?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 200" width="100%" height="auto" style="max-width:330px;display:block;margin:0 auto"><polygon points="150.0,20.0 100.0,180.0 200.0,180.0" fill="#dbeafe" fill-opacity="0.7" stroke="#3b4ea8" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

questions.hint: Imagine folding the shape: how many different fold lines make the two halves match?

steps.explain: A line of symmetry is a fold line: when you fold the shape along it, the two halves match exactly. Look at the isosceles triangle.
Try the first fold line (red dashed). The part on one side (orange) lands exactly on the other side.

questions.hint: Multiply each side length by the scale factor.

steps.explain: Area scales by the square of the length scale factor.
